info.title: haau3 Platform API
info.description: The haau3 platform API is in preview: it may change as we build, usually to add features or improve performance. Endpoints require an API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Requests without a valid key return 401. Create a key in the dashboard at https://platform.haau3.com; a new organization starts on the free Developer plan. From 2026-11-02 a request past one of its plan's limits (requests a minute on every plan, requests a month on Developer) returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Every service is on the FHIR R4 base at `/v1/fhir/r4`, and every error is a FHIR `OperationOutcome`; https://docs.haau3.com/errors lists every status, whether to retry it, and what a method a path does not take answers.

tags.name: FHIR base
tags.description: What the FHIR R4 base at `/v1/fhir/r4` answers for every service on it: the `CapabilityStatement` that lists them all, and batch Bundles that carry several requests to any of them in one round trip.

tags.name: Scheduling
tags.description: Provider availability from SMART Scheduling Links publishers: Slot and Schedule, searched and read, and the Location, Practitioner, PractitionerRole and HealthcareService they name.

tags.name: Terminology
tags.description: FHIR terminology operations over the code systems listed in TerminologyCapabilities. Some are resolved from their own source when you ask; others are held here at a named release, which that resource also names.

tags.name: Provider directory
tags.description: CMS's National Provider Directory as FHIR R4: practitioners and their roles, organizations, payers and insurance networks, network membership, healthcare services, locations and endpoints. Every parameter the service serves is declared here, and any other is refused by name rather than ignored.

tags.name: Questionnaires
tags.description: FHIR Questionnaire, served as its source publishes it. This service holds copies of a curated set and reaches any other questionnaire its source publishes by canonical URL, as well as forms published at their own address under places this service is set up to reach. Read one by id, and build the QuestionnaireResponse in your own application.

tags.name: Medical Benefits
tags.description: FHIR InsurancePlan: what a Medicare Advantage or ACA Marketplace plan covers and what a member pays, read from the files CMS publishes. Every plan names the CMS release it was read from. Read a plan by its id, or search by identifier, name, state or county, and check whether the CMS National Provider Directory lists providers in a plan's network.

tags.name: Pharmacy Benefits
tags.description: The CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check as FHIR messaging: what a medication would cost a member under their coverage, or its price at pharmacies near a ZIP code, in real time, from the sources this service connects to. A member's request receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement.

tags.name: MedList
tags.description: One reconciled medication list from one patient's FHIR medication records, as US Core MedicationRequests with a Provenance for each. This operation receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement.

tags.name: Structured Sig
tags.description: A prescription's free-text directions as a FHIR Dosage: the dose, unit, route, method and timing coded in SNOMED CT, NCIt and UCUM where the words support them, the directions kept verbatim, and a review flag on anything a person should check. It takes the directions and the medication's codings, never a patient.

tags.name: Sandbox
tags.description: The FHIR base without production behind it, to build and test against: the same paths at `/v1/sandbox/fhir/r4`, answered with synthetic data that always gives the same answer. Its first service is the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check, answered by Example Health Plan, a test insurer. It takes a test key (`haau3_sk_test_…`), made on the API keys page. A test key's requests count toward its organization's requests a minute, apart from its production requests, and never toward the plan's month. Send test members only, never a real person.

get.description: FHIR `[base]/metadata`. Returns the `CapabilityStatement` for this service, or a `TerminologyCapabilities` when called with `?mode=terminology`, which lists the code systems served and names those that are recognised but not served. `mode` is the only parameter it takes.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pass `terminology` for a `TerminologyCapabilities` resource instead of the `CapabilityStatement`. `full`, the default, returns the `CapabilityStatement`. No other mode is served.

200.description: A FHIR `CapabilityStatement`, or a `TerminologyCapabilities` when `mode=terminology`.

implementation.description: haau3 platform FHIR R4 API. Five services and three operations are served from this one base: terminology (CodeSystem, ValueSet), the provider directory (Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, OrganizationAffiliation, HealthcareService, Location, Endpoint), questionnaires (Questionnaire), Medical Benefits (InsurancePlan), Scheduling (Slot, Schedule, and a scheduling publisher's Location, Practitioner, PractitionerRole and HealthcareService, read by id), MedList's reconcile-medications, Pharmacy Benefits' process-message and Structured Sig's structure-dosage. Note that `/v1/` versions the haau3 platform API contract, not FHIR; the FHIR release is `r4`, and is echoed on every response as the `fhirVersion` media-type parameter.

rest.documentation:
All operations accept GET with query parameters and POST with a Parameters resource. Complex inputs — coding, and codeableConcept on the validate-code operations — are accepted on POST only, as the operations framework requires; on GET pass system and code as separate parameters. A codeableConcept validates if ANY of its codings is a member, which fits data whose elements carry a vendor-local coding alongside a standard one; per-coding membership deliberately ignores each coding's display (a wrong label must not veto a right code — display checking is available on the single-coding form). A coding's version is honoured where the operation defines a version parameter (the CodeSystem operations); ValueSet validation always uses the current code-system version and refuses a versioned coding rather than silently ignoring it. A coding whose system disagrees with an explicitly supplied system or url parameter is refused. Value sets and code systems are addressed by canonical url only; instance-level operation paths ([type]/[id]/$operation) are not offered. On $expand, displayLanguage, includeDesignations and activeOnly are refused by name. filter, count and offset narrow a value set this service hosts and the value sets of the code systems it holds (RxNorm and ICD-10-CM), and are refused for a value set resolved from its own source, which is returned whole. On the value sets of a held code system filter is required, the first 20 matches come back when count is not sent, and expansion.total is the exact number of matches; ICD-10-CM codes are written dotted (E11.9), and a header is a code marked notSelectable; how filter matches is in the TerminologyCapabilities (metadata?mode=terminology), expansion.textFilter. A batch Bundle POSTed to the base runs several operations in one round trip; each entry succeeds or fails independently.

Provider directory resources are proxied from the CMS National Provider Directory and served as published, without modification. Pharmacies, which the directory does not serve yet, come from NPPES, CMS's NPI Registry, through CMS's monthly and weekly files, updated weekly, and are served as NDH 2.0.0 models them: a HealthcareService with category `pharm`, its organization and its store (a pharmacy search on HealthcareService). Search is GET only. Every search parameter is either declared here or refused by name: a parameter this service does not serve is never silently ignored. Where the directory requires a parameter to be sent beside another (`network` on PractitionerRole and HealthcareService), the rule is applied here, before the directory is asked.

A curated set of questionnaires is served from copies vendored at a recorded release of their source, so those forms render the same way on every request. A search that names a canonical URL this service holds no copy of is answered from the source directly, and depends on that source being reachable. A search with no parameters lists the curated set. Search is GET only, and every search parameter is either declared here or refused by name. No operations are served on Questionnaire, and no QuestionnaireResponse is accepted or stored: a completed response is built by the application that collected it and references the questionnaire as `{url}|{version}`.

Medical Benefits (InsurancePlan): what a Medicare Advantage or ACA Marketplace plan covers and what a member pays, read from the files CMS publishes. Each plan conforms to the haau3 Medical Benefits profile (https://haau3.com/fhir/StructureDefinition/haau3-insurance-plan) and to the SBC InsurancePlan profile of the CARIN Digital Insurance Card guide, 2.0.0-ballot, and names the CMS release it was read from.

Scheduling: open appointment slots from SMART Scheduling Links publishers, each served as its publisher published it, with a new id, the publisher's own id in identifier and its address in meta.source. Search and read Slot and Schedule; a search brings each match's Schedule, Location and provider by _include.

MedList: POST [base]/$reconcile-medications reconciles one patient's medication records into one clean list, returned as a Bundle of reconciled MedicationRequests with a Provenance for each. The operation receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged. It is invoked directly and is not offered inside a batch.

Pharmacy Benefits: POST [base]/$process-message answers a pharmacy benefit check of the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check: what a medication would cost a member under their coverage (event rtpbc-request), or its price at pharmacies near a ZIP code, without patient details (event rtpbc-request-non-phi). A member's request carries patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged. It is invoked directly and is not offered inside a batch.

Structured Sig: POST [base]/$structure-dosage turns one prescription's free-text directions into a FHIR R4 Dosage, returned in a Parameters resource, with a review flag on anything a person should check. It takes the directions and, optionally, the medication's codings, never a patient. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged. It may also be sent inside a batch.

searchParam.name: identifier
searchParam.documentation: An NPI, as `{system}|{npi}` or a bare 10-digit value. Accepted systems: http://terminology.hl7.org/NamingSystem/npi, http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi, urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.6. All of them resolve the same provider. Responses carry the directory's own system, `http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi`, which may differ from the one you sent. One NPI per search; use a batch Bundle to resolve several. Any other identifier system is refused by name rather than searched, because a system the source does not index would answer with an empty result that reads as 'no such provider'.

searchParam.documentation: Matches across the whole name.

searchParam.name: family

searchParam.name: given

resource.documentation: Search by NPI to resolve an identifier you already hold, or by name to find one. A search needs an identifier, a name or an id: `address-city`, `address-state` and `active` narrow a search but cannot stand alone. Resources are served as the source publishes them, unmodified. Add `_revinclude=PractitionerRole:practitioner` to get the practitioner's roles in the same bundle. A scheduling publisher's Practitioner is also read here, by its id, `Practitioner-scheduling-` and 32 hexadecimal characters, and arrives as an included resource in a Slot or Schedule search. It is not found by searching this type.

A search needs a practitioner, organization, location, endpoint or id; `specialty`, `new-patient` and `active` narrow it. `network` and `new-patient-from-network` need a practitioner, organization, location or specialty beside them. `identifier` is not offered because the source does not carry identifiers on these resources. The directory records networks by the text of their type rather than a code; this service searches that text and confirms each answer is a network, and answers 502 rather than serve one that is not. A NUCC provider taxonomy code is refused: the directory's organizations carry none, and pharmacies are searched as `HealthcareService` (`service-category=pharm`).

searchParam.name: service-category
searchParam.documentation: `pharm`, bare or as `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/ndh-healthcare-service-category|pharm`: every pharmacy, of any kind. Starts a pharmacy search, as `specialty` does. A pharmacy search needs any one of: `location.address-postalcode` (a ZIP code or its first two or more digits), `location.address-state`, `name`, or one pharmacy's `organization` or `organization.identifier`. `location.address-city` narrows a search by state.

searchParam.name: specialty
searchParam.documentation: A NUCC pharmacy code, bare or as `http://nucc.org/provider-taxonomy|{code}`, or several separated by commas to find pharmacies of any of those kinds: for example `3336C0003X` (community or retail) or `3336M0002X` (mail order). Starts a pharmacy search. A pharmacy may carry only the general code 333600000X or only a specific one, so send `333600000X,3336C0003X` to find either, or `service-category=pharm` for every kind. Only pharmacy codes (333600000X, 3336C0002X, 3336C0003X, 3336C0004X, 3336H0001X, 3336I0012X, 3336L0003X, 3336M0002X, 3336M0003X, 3336N0007X, 3336S0011X, 332000000X, 332100000X, 332800000X) are served. A pharmacy search needs any one of: `location.address-postalcode` (a ZIP code or its first two or more digits), `location.address-state`, `name`, or one pharmacy's `organization` or `organization.identifier`. `location.address-city` narrows a search by state.

searchParam.name: location.address-state
searchParam.documentation: A pharmacy search's state: the two-letter code of the state the pharmacy's store is in. Stands alone on a pharmacy search, and is required beside `location.address-city`.

searchParam.name: location.address-postalcode
searchParam.documentation: Finds the pharmacies whose store's ZIP code starts with this: a ZIP code, ZIP+4, or its first two or more digits. Stands alone on a pharmacy search.

searchParam.name: location.address-city
searchParam.documentation: Narrows a pharmacy search to stores in a city whose name starts with this, so `Miami` also finds Miami Beach. Two or more letters. Send it with `location.address-state`.

searchParam.name: name
searchParam.documentation: Finds the pharmacies whose name, or a name they do business as, starts with this. Two or more letters. Stands alone on a pharmacy search.

searchParam.name: organization
searchParam.documentation: One pharmacy: the organization that provides it, as a pharmacy search returned it (`Organization-pharmacy-{NPI}`). Stands alone on a pharmacy search. Give a Organization id, `Organization/{id}`, or the `fullUrl` this service returned. An address on another server is refused.

searchParam.name: organization.identifier
searchParam.documentation: One pharmacy by its NPI, as `{system}|{npi}` or a bare 10-digit value, under the same systems `Organization` accepts. Stands alone on a pharmacy search.

searchParam.documentation: `true` or `false`. Narrows a search; cannot be used on its own. On a pharmacy search, `true` keeps the pharmacies NPPES lists as active and `false` the ones it lists as deactivated since its November 2026 monthly file; without it, both are returned, each marked by `active`.

resource.documentation: Two searches. The directory's services: its service records name a network and, for a few, a location; none names an organization. That search needs a location or an id, and `network` needs a location beside it. And pharmacies, modelled as NDH 2.0.0 models them: a pharmacy service (category `pharm`, its NUCC codes as `specialty`) provided by an organization at a store. A pharmacy search starts with `service-category=pharm` or a NUCC pharmacy `specialty`. A pharmacy search needs any one of: `location.address-postalcode` (a ZIP code or its first two or more digits), `location.address-state`, `name`, or one pharmacy's `organization` or `organization.identifier`. `location.address-city` narrows a search by state. Results come in one fixed order, the pharmacy's name ignoring case and then its NPI, the same on every page, and the searchset carries `total`. A continuation goes on in that order from the last pharmacy shown, so the weekly update does not cut a search short. Pharmacies come from NPPES, CMS's NPI Registry, through CMS's monthly and weekly files, updated weekly, until CMS's National Provider Directory serves them. Each resource's `meta.source` names the CMS file its record came from, which may no longer open once CMS removes it, and its `lastSourceSync` extension on `meta` the last day of NPPES data the answer holds. Each pharmacy is found and served at its primary practice address. A pharmacy's three ids, its service's, its organization's (`Organization-pharmacy-{NPI}`) and its store's, are read back from the same records, so a search and a read return the same record; they would change if the search moved to the directory. `Organization-{NPI}` is the directory's own record of an organization. A pharmacy NPPES lists as deactivated is served marked `active: false`, with its deactivation date, if it was deactivated since NPPES's November 2026 monthly file, and `active=true` asks for active pharmacies only. A pharmacy's ids are read by id; the directory's own searches refuse them. A scheduling publisher's HealthcareService is also read here, by its id, `HealthcareService-scheduling-` and 32 hexadecimal characters, and arrives as an included resource in a Slot or Schedule search. It is not found by searching this type.

get.description:
Search the Schedules of SMART Scheduling Links publishers: each the provider, the place and the service a publisher's Slots belong to. The answer is a FHIR `searchset` Bundle whose matches are Schedules, each as its publisher published it (the guide's Schedule profile), in order of id. Search `HealthcareService` two ways.

**The directory's services**, by location, or by network beside a location. The directory's service records name a network and, for a few, a location; none names an organization, so `organization` is refused on this search rather than answered with nothing.

**Pharmacies**, modelled as NDH 2.0.0 models them: each match is a pharmacy service, with category `pharm` and its NUCC pharmacy codes as `specialty`, provided by an organization at a store. Start the search with `service-category=pharm` (every kind) or `specialty` (one kind or several, separated by commas). A pharmacy search needs any one of: `location.address-postalcode` (a ZIP code or its first two or more digits), `location.address-state`, `name`, or one pharmacy's `organization` or `organization.identifier`. `location.address-city` narrows a search by state. Add `_include=HealthcareService:organization` and `_include=HealthcareService:location` to get each pharmacy's organization (its NPI) and store (its address) in the same bundle.

Results come in one fixed order, the pharmacy's name ignoring case and then its NPI, the same on every page, and the searchset carries `total`. A continuation goes on in that order from the last pharmacy shown, so the weekly update does not cut a search short. Pharmacies come from NPPES, CMS's NPI Registry, through CMS's monthly and weekly files, updated weekly, until CMS's National Provider Directory serves them. Each resource's `meta.source` names the CMS file its record came from, which may no longer open once CMS removes it, and its `lastSourceSync` extension on `meta` the last day of NPPES data the answer holds. Each pharmacy is found and served at its primary practice address. A pharmacy's three ids, its service's, its organization's (`Organization-pharmacy-{NPI}`) and its store's, are read back from the same records, so a search and a read return the same record; they would change if the search moved to the directory. `Organization-{NPI}` is the directory's own record of an organization. A pharmacy NPPES lists as deactivated is served marked `active: false`, with its deactivation date, if it was deactivated since NPPES's November 2026 monthly file, and `active=true` asks for active pharmacies only. A pharmacy's ids are read by id; the directory's own searches refuse them. One store can bill under more than one NPI, and each is served as its own pharmacy.

get.description:
Search the Medicare Advantage and ACA Marketplace plans being served, by identifier, name, or the state or county a plan is sold in. A search needs at least one of `identifier`, a form of `name`, `coverage-area-state` or `coverage-area-county`; `type` and `sold-to` narrow a search but are not one. Every result is the whole plan, sorted by name and then id, and every page states the total. Follow the `next` link to continue.

A plan sold in only part of a county matches the whole county. `GET /v1/fhir/r4/InsurancePlan/$counties?state=FL` lists a state's counties and their codes.

Every other parameter is refused by name rather than ignored, so a search never quietly answers a different question than the one asked. `address-state` and `address-postalcode` are refused with a pointer to the coverage-area parameters, because in FHIR R4 they search a plan's contact address.

Drug-only and dental-only plans are not served. An identifier search that finds one answers no plan and an `OperationOutcome` entry saying why.

get.description: FHIR instance-level operation `$in-network` on InsurancePlan: for each `npi`, whether the CMS National Provider Directory lists the provider in a network this plan names, for the plan's year; for each `pharmacy`, whether the plan's pharmacy network in CMS's Medicare Part D files for the month given lists the pharmacy. Give `npi`, `pharmacy` or both. The answer is a `Parameters` resource: the `plan`; the directory's `data-date`; one `network` per network checked, with the number of organizations it lists; a `reason` when there is no network data; a Marketplace plan's own `directory`; one `provider` per NPI, in the order sent, with its `status` (`in-network`, `not-found`, `not-in-directory` or `no-network-data`) and, when listed, `evidence` references to the directory's records on this base; then, for pharmacies, the `pharmacy-data-date` (the month the Part D file covers, `2026-11`), a `pharmacy-reason` when the plan has no Part D pharmacy network data, and one `pharmacy` per pharmacy NPI, in the order sent, with its `status` (`in-network`, `not-listed` or `no-network-data`) and, when listed, `retail`, `mail-order`, `preferred-retail` and `preferred-mail-order` as CMS's file states them; then a `source` for each source read. `not-found` never means out of network: the directory's network data is incomplete, and a listing is not a statement of a contract. `not-listed` is the Part D file's answer: it lists every retail and mail-order pharmacy in the plan's network for the month, and no other kind. A stand-alone prescription drug plan answers pharmacies only. All or nothing: a lookup that fails fails the whole answer. GET only. post.summary: Check what a medication costs (pharmacy benefit check)
post.description: FHIR system-level operation `$process-message`, as the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check (STU2 ballot, `2.0.0-ballot`) specifies. Not yet open to customers: while its price sources are being licensed, every request from a customer's organization, with or without patient details, is refused with `403` `forbidden`. POST a FHIR `Bundle` of type `message` whose first entry is a MessageHeader with one of two events. `rtpbc-request-non-phi` asks for a medication's price without patient details: a Claim naming the product (an NDC of 11 digits with no dashes, or an RxNorm code) and the quantity, with the patient and the coverage masked, and a pharmacy, up to three ZIP codes, or both. It is answered by the cash-price sources haau3 connects to, each named in the notes on its prices. `rtpbc-request` asks what a medication would cost a member under their coverage: the member's Patient and Coverage, with the payer's identifier in `payor.identifier`, the prescription and its prescriber, and a pharmacy. It is answered by the member's insurer, found by the payer's Payer ID: a `payor.identifier` whose `type` is `payerid` from `http://hl7.org/fhir/us/carin-bb/CodeSystem/C4BBIdentifierType`. An insurer that answers only with the member's own authorization is sent the access token from the member's login with that insurer, in the `Payer-Authorization` header, for that one request; it is never stored, logged or sent anywhere else. No insurer is connected yet. The answer is a `message` Bundle whose MessageHeader answers the request's, with one ClaimResponse that carries either prices and coverage in `item` or the reason there are none in `error`, and for a member's request the request's Patient as it was sent. With prices, `item` is the lowest price at a pharmacy near the ZIP codes or at the pharmacy named, every price is also an `addItem` alternative naming its pharmacy by an Organization in the Bundle and its price source in `programCode`, from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/pharmacy-benefits-price-source`, and `processNote` says where each price came from, when, and which free discount card pays it. Each price repeats the request's product coding, which CARIN requires to carry a display: an RxNorm code sent without one is answered with the display haau3's RxNorm release gives it, and an NDC needs its display sent with it. A check no connected source can answer carries `no-responder-for-coverage`, `no-price-source` or `source-not-available-to-caller` from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/pharmacy-benefits-processing-code`, and a member's request to an insurer that needs the member's authorization carries `payer-authorization-required` when none was sent and `payer-authorization-rejected` when the insurer refused it. A member's request the insurer declines under its own rules carries `insurer-declined-request`, and sending it again gives the same answer. An insurer that prices by NDC is asked about the request's NDC, or, for an RxNorm code, an NDC haau3's RxNorm release holds for the code or one of its branded forms, named in the answer's note; with none held it is not asked and the answer carries `ndc-required`, so send the NDC. Send the prescription's days supply in `MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.expectedSupplyDuration`, as a whole number of days with the UCUM code `d`; any other days supply is refused with `400`, and an insurer that requires one is not asked about a request without one: the answer carries `days-supply-required`, beside `ndc-required` when the NDC is missing too. A price is an estimate; the pharmacy confirms the price. A member's request receives patient data, so send real patient data only under an executed business associate agreement (BAA) on the Team or Scale plan. Without both, send a member's request only as test data marked as such, the request and every resource in it labelled with the `meta.security` coding `HTEST` from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-ActReason`; anything else is refused with `403` `phi-agreement-required`. A request without patient details needs neither. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged, apart from the request's ids, and every answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The operation takes no query parameters and is not offered inside a batch. The contract is published at https://fhir.haau3.com/pharmacy-benefits.html.

parameters.name: Payer-Authorization
parameters.description: A member's own authorization at their insurer, for a member's request (event `rtpbc-request`) to an insurer that answers only with it: `Bearer` and the access token your app obtained from the member's login with that insurer, as an `Authorization` header carries one. It is forwarded once, to that insurer, for this request, and is never stored, logged or sent anywhere else. Without it, such a request is answered `payer-authorization-required`; a token the insurer refuses is answered `payer-authorization-rejected`. A request without patient details that carries it is refused.

post.summary: Structure a prescription's directions as a FHIR Dosage
post.description: FHIR system-level operation `$structure-dosage`. POST a Parameters resource with one `text` part, a prescription's directions as written, at most 1,000 characters, and optionally one `medication` part, the medication's codings as a CodeableConcept (RxNorm or NDC). The answer is a Parameters resource with one `dosage` part: a FHIR Dosage conforming to haau3 Structured Dosage, whose `text` is the directions exactly as sent and whose dose and unit, route, method, timing and as-needed elements are coded where the words support them, in SNOMED CT (Global Patient Set concepts only), NCIt and UCUM. Nothing is invented: an element the directions do not support is absent. Anything a person should check is a review flag on the Dosage, an extension with a code from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/structured-sig-review-flag` and, when the flag is about words, those words. Every Dosage names the engine and vocabulary versions it was written under, and the RxNorm release when the medication's code was looked up. With an RxNorm code, the product's dose form checks the dose's unit and the route, and supplies either when the directions name none, each flagged. Send the directions and the medication's codings only, never a patient's name or identifiers. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged, apart from the request's ids, and every answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The operation takes no query parameters, and may be sent inside a batch, one request per entry. The contract is published at https://fhir.haau3.com/OperationDefinition-structure-dosage.html.

post.summary: Check a test member's medication cost with a test insurer
post.description: The Sandbox's pharmacy benefit check: the same operation as `/v1/fhir/r4/$process-message`, reading, routing and answering a request as it does, at the Sandbox's FHIR base, `/v1/sandbox/fhir/r4`, where Example Health Plan, a test insurer, answers the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check (STU2 ballot, `2.0.0-ballot`) as a payer would, with synthetic data, and nothing real answers. Every organization may call it on every plan, with no business associate agreement and no `HTEST` label, since only its test insurer can answer; production needs both for a member's request. A test key's requests count toward its organization's requests a minute, apart from its production requests, and never toward the plan's month. Send a test key (`haau3_sk_test_…`): a live key is refused with `live-key-in-sandbox`. POST a FHIR `Bundle` of type `message` whose first entry is a MessageHeader with one of two events. `rtpbc-request` is a member's request, with the member's Patient and Coverage, the prescription and its prescriber, and a pharmacy. It is routed by the payer's Payer ID, a `payor.identifier` whose `type` is `payerid` from `http://hl7.org/fhir/us/carin-bb/CodeSystem/C4BBIdentifierType`, as production routes it: `SANDBOX-EHP`, or the guide's example payer `EXAMPLE-PAYER`, reaches Example Health Plan, and any other Payer ID, or a payer named without one, is answered `no-responder-for-coverage` and no one is asked. Example Health Plan answers its test members only, named by member ID in `Coverage.subscriberId`, the Coverage's `rxid` class, or a Patient identifier whose system is `https://example-health-plan.test/member-id`; a request for anyone else is answered the error `no-test-member` and nothing else. Send test members only, never a real person. Each medication in the test insurer's formulary table always gets the same answer, by its RxNorm code or NDC: priced with a copay, covered at $0 with an alternative, not covered with an alternative, prior authorization required, or a quantity limit. Any other medication gets a default priced answer, and one test member's requests are always declined, `insurer-declined`. Both errors are coded from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/sandbox-error` in `ClaimResponse.error`. `rtpbc-request-non-phi` is the request without patient details, read as production reads it and answered `no-price-source`, since no price source is connected; it and `no-responder-for-coverage` are coded from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/pharmacy-benefits-processing-code`. The answer is a `message` Bundle whose MessageHeader answers the request's, with one ClaimResponse and, for a member's request, the request's Patient as it was sent; the test insurer's answer names it by its Payer ID, `SANDBOX-EHP`, and its process notes say which test member and formulary row answered, and when. Amounts are fixed, whatever the quantity. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged, and every answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The operation takes no query parameters. The test members and the formulary table are at https://docs.haau3.com/sandbox/example-health-plan. Deprecated: call `processMessage` on the Sandbox's own host, `https://sandbox.haau3.com`, with a test key or none. It takes the same request and gives the same answers. This address is removed once it has gone 14 days without a call, with a changelog entry that day.
